{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZbmSxw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDC4Ys", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 83, "title": "Distinguish stable correspondent identities from handles throughout local mail", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `fb89fca3c0d0e4bc6cfdbb80a8b72ac81ae976da`, mail resolves and stores stable member identities but loses that distinction in its presentation:

- `src/mail.ts:14` shows only the correspondent's handle in INBOX/SENT rows.
- `src/mail.ts:17–18` shows only handles for both letter parties.
- `src/commands.ts:150` passes only `recipient.handle` into `TerminalComposer`; its opening and review screens therefore cannot distinguish recipients sharing a handle.
- `MEMBERS` shows stable short addresses and handles, but does not connect them to the synthetic identity already used in forums and OLT.

Consequently, two correspondents with identical handles look alike even after successful address resolution. Renames also remove the visible connection between earlier interactions and the same account. This is an existing presentation gap, not a demonstrated regression from the latest NetNews merge.

## Expected outcome

Mail lists, both letter-header parties and draft recipient presentation show the member's existing stable synthetic token separately from the safe current handle. `MEMBERS` connects that token and handle to the existing usable short address.

A user can recognize a resident across forum, OLT and mail; select the correct address despite duplicate handles; verify the resolved recipient before sending; and recognize the same correspondent after a rename. Preserve all routing and storage behavior.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction

Sources were inspected live on 2026-10-24:

- The participant reference explicitly describes registered nicknames replacing real names in mail's displayed name field. Confidence is high in the page's statement, moderate for historical applicability because the practice is undated. It does not establish that names replaced account identifiers or authenticate a 1996 header. Add no real-name field or requirement. [PC-VAN participant reference](https://www2s.biglobe.ne.jp/nozomin/kanri/pcvan.html)
- The October 1994 mail article documents ID-based intra-PC-VAN addressing separately from external address conventions. This supports distinguishing an address from a personal display name, with an explicit continuity assumption for 1996. It supplies no target-year header layout. Other services' illustrated controls must remain separate. [Internet Magazine, October 1994, pp. 106–107](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199410-104-bbs.pdf)
- The reproduced judgment dated December 22, 1997 describes earlier PC-VAN activity involving separate IDs and handles, including mail. This is corroboration of the conceptual distinction, not evidence for mail-header geometry. Historical confidence is moderate: the publisher disclaims guaranteed accuracy/authenticity, and the original and omitted annex remain unavailable. [Judgment transcription](https://www.law.co.jp/cases/pcvan.htm)
- November 1996 documentation separately identifies Internet-mail addressing through `INET#`. It does not authenticate local composer controls or header placement. This correction must not imply that the historical service lacked Internet mail. [Internet Magazine, November 1996, p. 221](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199611-220-mail2.pdf)

**Accepted reconstruction:** extend the existing forum/OLT `SYN-…` labels into mail using `src/member-presentation.ts:identityToken` and `penName` unchanged. Placement, delimiters, short local addresses and current-name refresh are category D product choices, not recovered 1996 host formatting. Confidence is high in the implementation defect and feasibility, moderate in the historical identity/name distinction, and low in any exact mail layout. Already printed scrollback need not change after a rename.

### Implementation and history

`resolveMailResident` already rejects ambiguous handles and prioritizes existing stable addresses. `createHumanMail` pins the resolved recipient ID. Reuse these behaviors; a display token must not introduce a new addressing mechanism. A small presentation change needs no schema migration or new identity registry.

For reproduction, use a deterministic local fixture with two existing residents sharing a handle. Address each by its short address, review and send a letter, then inspect SENT and each letter. Current output repeats the same handle; expected output distinguishes the residents with their existing cross-service tokens. Include received mail and REPLY in validation using valid fixtures or existing mocked generation.

Live repository searches returned no open Issues or PRs. [Mail #52](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/52), [forum identity #71](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/71) and [OLT identity #79](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/79) are closed as completed; this extends their existing conventions into the remaining mail surfaces.

[PR #82](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/82) and `docs/validation.md` record 282 passing checks, including configured type checking and production build. Those are Coordinator-reported results, not checks run by this research graph. The returned PR review list was empty; that does not establish absence of review elsewhere.

Scope excludes conference attribution, sender-read lifecycle, current/old/SIG mailbox migration, Internet-mail implementation and command-history reconstruction.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Use the unchanged shared token/name helpers for INBOX/SENT correspondents, both parties in READ, and the resolved recipient in composer opening and review output, including REPLY. Apply consistently through MAIN `1`, MAIN `X` and SIG `MAIL`, preserving their entry and return contexts.
- [ ] Extend `MEMBERS` to associate each available resident's existing short address, matching synthetic token and safe handle. Keep addressing discoverable without advertising `SYN-…` as an address. Preserve stable-address precedence, exact-handle resolution, ambiguous-handle rejection and recipient-ID pinning through review, editing and save retry.
- [ ] Preserve the existing token algorithm and namespace. Tokens survive human/resident renames, member-array reordering, reload and JSON restore. Re-rendered lists/details show current safe names; drafts retain the identity selected at creation. Duplicate handles remain distinguishable without introducing stored display fields.
- [ ] Reuse conservative name fallbacks. Unresolved renderer references show `不明`/`名無し`, and unusable names use `名無し`; do not expose technical keys as attribution or invent members. Do not extend the forum-only DEMO exception into mail. Invalid reference imports must still fail existing validation.
- [ ] Preserve literal subjects/bodies and whitespace, member/mail IDs, routing, numbering, reply links, timestamps/calendar projection and mailbox visibility. Keep normal human-recipient read marking unchanged; display calculation adds no writes or invented resident-read events. Preserve consent, private-context isolation, activity scheduling, cancellation and import/reset fences.
- [ ] Add focused coverage with the existing Playwright setup for duplicate handles, human/resident renames, both letter parties, new/reply recipient confirmation, directory-to-token matching, safe fallbacks and unchanged source records. Cover token stability across reordering and backup/restore. Update obsolete handle-only assertions while retaining exact Japanese text, literal markup, quota retry, idempotent send, cancellation, IME and terminal regressions.
- [ ] Include a production keyboard journey using duplicate-handle residents: MEMBERS → stable-address WRITE → review/EDIT → send → SENT/READ, plus received READ → REPLY → recipient review. Exercise all three mail routes and verify reload/restore stability. Use deterministic fixtures or mocked inference; no real model, download, GPU, remote delivery or human approval is needed.
- [ ] Update `docs/mail.md`, the research record and relevant README/Settings/About descriptions. Record source URLs, inspection date, confidence and reconstruction assumptions. Keep provenance in existing documentation/About surfaces, with concise ordinary terminal output.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test`, whose existing Playwright configuration includes TypeScript checking and production bundling, and records actual results. Review the complete diff, affected documentation links and `git diff --check`. Use existing tooling and preserve functional, storage, consent, IME and terminal coverage.

## Optional validation

Additional readability comparison with a newly recovered dated mail transcript may refine spacing later. Native-IME, hardware and subjective historical-layout checks are not completion gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks can be completed before merge.
